title: Parking Reservations API
summary: Fix a boundary bug that refuses back-to-back bookings in a Spring Boot garage API, add availability search and cancellation, then keep search fast on a 240,000-reservation lot with an interval index.
overview:
You've joined **Parkwise**, which runs multi-level garages near stadiums and airports. Drivers book a space for a time window in the app, and the gate reads their plate when they arrive. This Spring Boot service owns the spaces and the reservations.

The codebase is layered the usual way: `controller/` maps HTTP to service calls, `service/` holds the rules (`ReservationService` for booking, `AvailabilityService` for search, `Windows` for time-window checks), `repository/` keeps everything in memory, `model/` has `Space`, `Reservation` and `VehicleSize`, `dto/` has the request and response records, and `exception/` turns errors into one JSON shape.

Start with `README.md`: it is the API contract, with the half-open window rule, cancellation, best-fit ordering, the status codes and the error shape. Then read `ReservationService`, `Reservation` and `ReservationRepository`. Services get "now" from an injected `Clock`.

phases.title: Back-to-back bookings refused
phases.instructions:
Garage managers have escalated a revenue problem:

> *"Our busiest spaces sit empty for whole time slots. A driver booked bay B-07 until 12:00, and the next driver who tried to book it from 12:00 got 'Space is already booked for part of that time'. The same happens the other way round: booking until 10:00 a space that is taken from 10:00 is refused."*

The README says windows are half-open: `[start, end)` holds the space up to, but not including, `end`. Bookings that only touch at an end point must both succeed (`201`), while bookings that really share time must still get `409 space_unavailable`.

**Done when** every test in `Phase1Test` passes. Write down the two windows that should not conflict before you change any code, and check your fix against windows that do overlap, contain or sit inside another.
hints: The refusal is a `409 space_unavailable`, so the conflict check runs and decides the windows overlap. Find where `ReservationService.reserve` asks that question.

Look at `Reservation.overlaps`. It is written as 'not (one ends before the other starts, or starts after the other ends)'. Which comparison is wrong for two windows that only touch, where one's `end` equals the other's `start`?

For half-open windows, `[a, b)` and `[c, d)` overlap exactly when `a < d && c < b`: `return otherStart.isBefore(end) && start.isBefore(otherEnd);`. `isBefore` is strict, so equal end points do not count as overlap.
phases.answer:
**Root cause.** `Reservation.overlaps` treated windows as closed intervals:

```java
return !(otherEnd.isBefore(start) || otherStart.isAfter(end));
```

When `otherEnd` equals `start`, `isBefore` is false (they are equal), so the negation reports an overlap. The same happens when `otherStart` equals `end`. Back-to-back bookings, the most common case in a busy garage, were all refused.

**Fix.** Use the half-open test, each window starting strictly before the other ends:

```java
return otherStart.isBefore(end) && start.isBefore(otherEnd);
```

**Verify.** Back-to-back windows in both directions now succeed, and overlapping, containing and contained windows still return `409`. Because availability search (phase 2) uses the same method, fixing it once in the model keeps booking and search consistent.

phases.title: Availability search and cancellation
phases.instructions:
Drivers need to find a space before they book one, and to cancel bookings they no longer need.

**1. `GET /availability?start=&end=&vehicleSize=`** (implement `AvailabilityService.findAvailable`). Return `{"count", "spaces"}` with every space that:

- the vehicle fits in (`vehicleSize.fitsIn(space.size())`), and
- has no **active** reservation overlapping `[start, end)`.

Sort best fit first: by space size (smallest first), then level (lowest first), then id. A missing parameter, an unreadable time or size, or a window that does not end after it starts is `422 validation_error` with the parameter in `fields` (the `Windows` helper already checks the window).

**2. `POST /reservations/{id}/cancel`** (implement `ReservationService.cancel`):

- `200` with the reservation, now `CANCELLED` with `cancelledAt` set.
- `404 reservation_not_found` for an unknown id; `409 already_cancelled` when it was cancelled before.
- `409 cancellation_closed` when it starts less than 30 minutes from now (`ReservationService.CANCELLATION_CUTOFF`), or has started. Use the injected `Clock`.
- A cancelled reservation no longer holds its space: it must not block new bookings or hide the space from search. Save the reservation after changing it.

**Done when** `Phase1Test` and `Phase2Test` pass.
hints: Search is a filter and a sort: for each space, check the size, then whether any of its active reservations overlaps the window. Reuse `Reservation.overlaps` so booking and search agree on what overlap means.

`Comparator.comparing(Space::size).thenComparingInt(Space::level).thenComparingLong(Space::id)` gives the best-fit order, because enums compare by declaration order. For cancellation, check the status first, then compare `clock.instant()` with `start.minus(CANCELLATION_CUTOFF)`.

Do not forget the booking path: `reserve` checks every reservation of the space for overlap, cancelled ones included. Add `existing.isActive() &&` to that check. Make `cancel` `synchronized` like `reserve`, so a cancel and a booking of the same space cannot interleave.
phases.answer:
**Search.** Validate the window with `Windows.check`, keep the spaces the vehicle fits, drop any space with an active reservation that overlaps `[start, end)`, and sort with `size, level, id`. With `S` spaces and `N` reservations in total this costs `O(S * N)` per search, because `findBySpace` scans every reservation for every space. That is fine for a demo garage and is what phase 3 fixes.

**Cancellation.** Look up the reservation (`404`), refuse a second cancel (`409 already_cancelled`), refuse when `now` is after `start - 30 minutes` (`409 cancellation_closed`), then `cancel(now)` and save it. Exactly 30 minutes before the start is still allowed. The time comes from the injected `Clock`, so a test could fix it.

**Cancelled bookings free the space.** Both `reserve` and search must ignore reservations that are not active. Forgetting the booking path is the classic slip: search shows the space as free, and booking it fails with `409`.

phases.title: Search on the big lot
phases.instructions:
Parkwise is moving its airport garage onto this service: 600 spaces with 400 reservations each, 240,000 in all. On that data the phase-2 search takes more than a second **per query**, and the app sends thousands of searches an hour.

Make availability search fast without changing its results:

- `Phase3Test` runs **3,000 searches in under 4 seconds** in total, for random windows and vehicle sizes.
- Results must match a brute-force check exactly, including windows that only touch a booking at an end point.
- Booking and cancelling must keep search current: a booked window disappears from the results, and a cancelled one comes back.
- Booking (`reserve`) must stay correct on the big lot too.

The test seeds the lot directly through `SpaceRepository.save` and `ReservationRepository.save`, then calls `AvailabilityService.findAvailable`. So whatever index you build must be maintained by `ReservationRepository.save` (which is also called after a cancellation), not by the service.

**Done when** all three test classes pass.
hints: The phase-2 search does `S` scans of all `N` reservations per query. First idea: group reservations by space so each space only looks at its own. That still checks all 400 reservations of every space. What property do one space's active reservations have that a sorted structure can exploit?

Active reservations on one space never overlap. Sorted by start, they are therefore also sorted by end. Keep a `NavigableMap<Instant, Reservation>` (a `TreeMap` or `ConcurrentSkipListMap`) per space, keyed by start, holding only active reservations. `save` adds active ones and removes cancelled ones.

To ask whether a space is free for `[start, end)`, only one reservation can conflict: the one with the latest start before `end`, which is `index.lowerEntry(end)`. Every earlier one ends no later than that one starts. The space is free if there is no such entry or it does not overlap the window. Use the same `isFree` check in `reserve`.
phases.answer:
**Why phase 2 is slow.** For each of the ~400 spaces a vehicle fits, `findBySpace` streams through all 240,000 reservations: about 10^8 checks per search, more than a second each. Grouping by space helps (400 checks per space), but still scans every booking of every space.

**Interval index.** `ReservationRepository` keeps, per space, a `ConcurrentSkipListMap<Instant, Reservation>` of active reservations keyed by start. `save` puts an active reservation and removes a cancelled one (`index.remove(start, reservation)`, so it only removes that exact entry). Because active reservations on a space are disjoint, they are sorted by end as well as by start, so `isFree(space, start, end)` needs one lookup:

```java
Map.Entry<Instant, Reservation> latest = index.lowerEntry(end);
return latest == null || !latest.getValue().overlaps(start, end);
```

A search is now `O(S log R)` for `S` spaces with `R` reservations each, a few hundred microseconds instead of a second or more. `reserve` uses the same `isFree` check under its lock, so booking and search agree, and the disjointness invariant the index relies on is the one `reserve` enforces.

**Tradeoffs.** The index costs one map entry per active reservation, and every write path must go through `save`; a reservation changed without saving would leave the index stale, which is why the README asks for it. A skip list keeps reads lock-free while `reserve` and `cancel` write. For richer queries ("free for at least 2 hours between 9 and 18"), an interval tree or a per-space bitmap of time slots would be the next step.

debrief: Why did the closed-interval overlap test refuse back-to-back bookings, and which windows did you use to prove your fix did not let real overlaps through?
How does your search order spaces, and where did you make sure cancelled reservations stop holding a space? What does a phase-2 search cost in terms of spaces and reservations?

Why is one `lowerEntry(end)` lookup enough to decide whether a space is free, and what invariant does that depend on? How did you check that the faster search returns exactly the same results as the slow one?
